questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A city where there was a lot to explore and a lot to do that was also financially possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had so many courses that it was hard to have the time or energy to get to see any of the things that I originally wanted moreover the workload did not match the workload I had in Denmark. I used a lot more time studying then I ever had, and since I had the expectation of going there to explore a new culture I was not very happy overall. Moreover there was a lot of imperfections at Charles university and at the Dorm I stayed that made it a lot worse all in all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not that hard to find the needed information in the start we simply wrote to our Coordinator.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was fine, not very clear however it was still fine.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The only option was sharing a small room with another person where you slept together, and each person had their own table, bed, and closet. Then you would share the kitchen and bathroom with 3 people in total, making it very hard to make food if anyone else was interested in doing that.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a small stove in the kitchen provided that was very bad, and a oven that you shared with everybody that you had to get approval to use each time you wanted to use it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is cheap and you get what you pay for. It is not something that you should do if you are not fine with living in "bad" housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its okay since its cheap but its really not "great" living.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to get your ISIC and then using you ISIC you can login into SIS and then on SIS you can register for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write to professors and ask to be able to take their course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 5 out of the 6 courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your ISIC quickly since local students can search for the courses before and some of the classes you might want to take are already full. If they are full then go to the waiting list, I was on the waiting list for almost all my courses and I only missed 1 of them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine, some of my courses where very well taught while others where much worse.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses match as the level as in UCPH however not in the amount of credits. The courses in Charles have taken a lot more of time and work to complete than they should for them being 5 credits per course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more hands on which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not made aware that there where any non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have no idea.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hang out with friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Pilsen, visit smaller cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There was not a large Culture shock or change that I noticed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People where more friendly than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: DO NOT TAKE TO MANY COURSES, Try meeting people from outside the university , Explore the city and try visiting the different Museums.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: 5 CREDITS DOES NOT MEAN A SHORTER OR EASIER COURSE THAN 7.5 CREDITS.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to complete so much work since I choose 6 courses that each where 5 credits. It was a LOT of work and took all my energy and time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
